_note: Outside powers. Phase 1 keeps these as pressure and chronicle names only; the engine need not load this file.

people.name: Himilcon
people.role: General of Carthage; made the peace of 405 and led the war of 397/396

facts.text: Fled Syracuse by night, about 396, after paying off Dionysius.
facts.quote: Himilcon during the night conveyed the three hundred talents to the acropolis
no less than eighty thousand in number and under the command of Magon

facts.text: The peace of 405 left Syracuse to Dionysius.
facts.quote: the Syracusans shall be subject to Dionysius

outside.name: Sparta
outside.role: A friend of the tyranny that poses as a friend of liberty

facts.text: Came to strengthen the tyranny while promising liberty.
facts.quote: ostensibly pretending that they would overthrow the government, but in truth with intent to increase the power of the tyranny

people.name: Pharacidas
people.role: Spartan admiral of the allied fleet, 396

facts.text: Blocked the move against Dionysius in the assembly.
facts.quote: he was on friendly terms with the tyrant

disputes: Diodorus 14.70.3 also names "Aretes the Lacedaemonian" who betrayed the Syracusans earlier. Whether he is Aristus is not settled in these texts.

outside.name: Catana, Naxos and Leontini, the nearby cities

people.name: Arcesilaus
people.role: General of Catana who betrayed it

facts.quote: Arcesilaüs, the general of the Catanians, had offered to betray the city

people.name: Procles
people.role: Commander of Naxos who betrayed it

facts.quote: Procles, the commander of the Naxians, on being won over by great promises

outside.name: The Italian Greeks
outside.role: Rhegium, Croton and the cities across the strait, a refuge for exiles

facts.text: Rhegium refused a marriage with Dionysius, about 398.
facts.quote: the Rhegians voted not to accept the marriage connection

facts.text: Croton sheltered the most Syracusan exiles.
facts.quote: had the largest number of exiles from Syracuse
